title: Deciding identities in all finite-dimensional subspace lattices
statement: For a fixed field \(F\), is there an algorithm deciding whether two finite terms in sum and intersection have equal values on every tuple of subspaces in every finite-dimensional \(F\)-vector space? The concrete proposed reduction is to dimension \(1+\min\{\max(d(p),d(q)),\max(k(p),k(q))\}\), where \(d\) and \(k\) count joins and meets in the written terms.
status: Solved by the speaker: \citet[Lemma~1, Lemmas~2--3 and main theorem]{ryzhikova1987decidability}; received May 1986, Russian publication 1987, English translation 1988. As of November 2026, the exact identity-decision problem is settled; no complexity or general first-order decidability claim is added.

title: Index formulas for elliptic Fuchs-type operators with conic ends
statement: For a cone-elliptic regular singular differential operator on a compact manifold with isolated conic ends, and a specified closed \(L^2\) domain between its minimal and maximal domains, express its index by interior data, Mellin-symbol spectral data, and the chosen indicial-domain contribution. This is a reconstruction of the notebook's general ``index?'' question; its printed operator and domain are incomplete.
status: Developed by others. \citet[Prop.~1.3.16 and Cor.~2.4.7]{lesch1997fuchs} proves Fredholmness and an index formula in the constant-near-tip setting; Thm.~2.4.8 specializes it for first-order operators. Habilitation submitted 1993; preprint 1996; book 1997. As of November 2026 this is an established formulation, not a claim that every unqualified regular singular expression has a canonical index.

title: Reducibility and first singular vectors of Virasoro Verma modules
statement: For \(h,c\in\mathbb C\), determine when the Virasoro Verma module \(M(h,c)\) is reducible and determine its first positive grade containing a singular vector. The central-generator convention must be fixed before comparing formulas.
status: Solved before the present talk. \citet[\S3.2, Thm.~3.1 and corollary]{feiginfuchs1982invariant} gives the determinant factors and the first-grade criterion. Received September 1981, published 1982. As of November 2026, this recurrence remains E; the 1985 notebook's \(1/2\) coefficient must be corrected to \(1/16\).
